business_scope.primary_industry_name: Cross-Border Trade Policy Analysis and Foreign Stakeholder Lobbying

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (Napoleonic Code) with hybrid EU regulatory layer (Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union supremacy) and public-administrative law traditions; corporate/AML matters are codified in the Commercial Code and Monetary and Financial Code.
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: France-US Tax Convention on Income and Capital (2009) - active
France-China Bilateral Investment and Tax Treaties (as amended, in force)
EU-Canada Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA) - provisional application in force
EU-Japan Economic Partnership Agreement (EPA) - in force
France-Germany Double Taxation Agreement (as amended by Additional Protocol of 2 July 2018) - active

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: French Monetary and Financial Code (Code monétaire et financier), Articles L.561-1 to L.561-50 and R.561-1 to R.561-31; Decree No. 2019-1069 of 21 October 2019 (register of beneficial owners); EU Directive (EU) 2015/849, as amended by (EU) 2018/843 (5AMLD), transposed by French Ordinance No. 2020-115 and Decree No. 2021-1532; French Commercial Code Articles L.123-832 to L.123-834 and R.123-221 to R.123-223 (UBO declaration with the RCS/RNE); General Tax Code (obligated entities and tax registration); Loi Sapin II (Law No. 2016-1691) for transparency in public-life/interest-representative activities; French AML/CFT Action Plan of 2022 and TRACFIN guidelines.
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_disclosure_level: Government_Only_Access (access restricted to public authorities and accredited AML/CFT institutions with a legitimate interest; not a fully public register after ECJ rulings C-37/20 and C-601/20; filings are stored in the French national companies register - RNE/INPI).

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of good standing / corporate extract of any corporate shareholder or UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Company registry / Chamber of Commerce in the country of incorporation of the corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille OR Consular Legalization for non-Hague jurisdictions

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Passport or national identity document of every manager (gérant) and each natural-person UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Home-country passport office, prefecture or competent ministry of interior
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (if issued by a Hague Convention state) OR Consular Legalization (non-Hague); plus court-certified French translation where the original is not in French or English

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank capital-deposit certificate (certificat de dépôt de fonds) or notary attestation of share-capital payment (if cash contribution)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: French credit institution, Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations, or French notary
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille not required; French domestic instrument must be in French and produced for the RCS filing

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of attorney (POA) or resolutory instrument, if the incorporation file is signed by a representative/agent
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Foreign notary or corporate board of directors/shareholders
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille OR Consular Legalization (if foreign); French notarization when the representative signs before a French notary

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of legalization/consular registration of the foreign shareholding entity (if governed by a non-Hague country)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: French consulate in the foreign country, plus competent local authority
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization (must be obtained before the French administration accepts the document)

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: French Commercial Code (Code de commerce), Articles L.223-1 to L.223-43 (SARL formation, operation and dissolution) and Articles L.123-1 et seq. and R.123-1 et seq. (registration with the Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés), as implemented by the Guichet unique formalities under Ordinance No. 2021-300 and Decree No. 2021-300.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) operated by the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce; receiving filings through the INPI Guichet unique des formalités des entreprises.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Déclaration de constitution de société submitted through the INPI online portal; accompanied by the attestation de parution in an authorized Journal d'annonces légales (JAL) and supporting constitutive documents.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital for a SARL under Article L.223-2 of the Code de commerce; articles may fix a higher threshold. If cash capital is used, the funds must be deposited and blocked in a French banking account, with a notary, or with the Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations, and the blockage certificate must be kept until RCS registration; in-kind contributions must be fully paid up and valued in the articles.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED first general meeting of the members: 1. Share Subscription: the member(s) subscribe in full the issued share capital, fully paid in accordance with the blocked funds certificate, and the shares are allotted. 2. Registered Office: the registered office is fixed at the address stated in the articles. 3. Officers: [Name] is appointed as Gérant with authority to bind the company, open bank accounts and complete registration formalities. 4. Ratification: all steps necessary for incorporation, legal publication, RCS filing and sector registration are ratified.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and Execution of Articles of Association and Governance Instruments
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Constituent members acting privately; optional civil-law notary for notarial execution (required for in-kind contributions).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the statuts in French, including company name, SARL legal form, duration not exceeding 99 years, registered office address, corporate object limited to public affairs consulting, trade policy analysis and interest representation, share capital, contribution details, share ownership and Gérant appointment. Execute all signature pages before depositing any capital; if a notary is used, sign the notarial minutes and provide proof of identity.
required_dossiers: Statuts en français executed by all members
Acte de nomination du gérant and signed acceptance
Valuation annex for in-kind contributions, if applicable
Proof of identity and address of each member and manager
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry or notary identifies missing or invalid clauses, amend the articles by a supplementary deed executed by all members and re-file the corrected version before proceeding further.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Deposit of Cash Capital and Obtaining Blockage Certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial bank in France, Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations, or civil-law notary.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary capital lock-up account designating the proposed company, transfer the full cash subscription, and obtain the attestation de blocage des fonds. The certificate must identify the subscribers, amount, date of deposit and account details. Retain the certificate for submission to the registry and release the funds to the definitive company account only after RCS registration, upon presentation of the K-bis extract and under Gérant signature.
required_dossiers: Cash subscription transfer confirmation or bank receipt
Bank acceptance of temporary capital lock-up account
Attestation de blocage des fonds
Identity and beneficial owner KYC documents for each subscriber
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank refuses the deposit due to KYC gaps, resubmit the documentation, open the account with an alternative regulated institution or deposit funds with the Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations and issue a fresh blockage certificate.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication of the Legal Notice in a Journal d'Annonces Légales
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Journal d'annonces légales (JAL) authorized in the département of the registered office.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Publish a legal announcement before RCS filing, containing the company name, SARL form, registered office address, capital amount, corporate object, duration, Gérant name and RCS registration city. Obtain the attestation de parution from the JAL. The notice must appear within the statutory window before the formal filing.
required_dossiers: Text of the legal announcement
JAL publication order form
Identity details of the Gérant
Registered office address and corporate purpose summary
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the JAL rejects the notice for incomplete information, correct the announcement, purchase a new insertion and resubmit the legal notice within the permitted period.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of the Incorporation Dossier with the RCS through the Guichet Unique
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: INPI Guichet unique des formalités des entreprises, transmitting files to the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce for RCS registration.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log in to the official Guichet unique portal, select company creation and the SARL legal form, complete the declaration forms, upload the executed statuts, blockage certificate, legal notice attestation, Gérant appointment and acceptance, registered office justification, and the declaration of beneficial owners. Pay any applicable registry fee via the portal and follow the online tracking; answer any registry queries directly in the same platform.
required_dossiers: Completed online declaration form
Signed and dated statuts file
Attestation de dépôt des fonds (blockage certificate)
Attestation de parution in the JAL
Acte de nomination du Gérant and acceptance document
Déclaration des bénéficiaires effectifs (DBE)
Proof of registered office occupancy (tenancy agreement, utility bill or free-of-charge authorization)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS issues a query or rejection, file a rectification within the prescribed deadline through the Guichet unique's regularization channel; provide the exact missing document or amend the statutes/deed; if the filing lapses, restart the formalities with a fresh full application.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtaining K-bis Extract, SIREN/SIRET and Tax and Social Registrations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce for K-bis; INSEE for SIREN; URSSAF for social security; DGFiP for tax accounts.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After the RCS issues the immatriculation certificate, retrieve the extrait K-bis, confirm the SIREN/SIRET numbers and the APE code 7020Z. Ensure that the K-bis address matches the registered office. Verify that URSSAF registration, French VAT number or eligibility status, and the tax office identification have been generated automatically through the formalities system; notify the bank and clients with official documentation.
required_dossiers: RCS registration certificate/acknowledgment
Extrait K-bis
SIREN/SIRET confirmation
URSSAF confirmation or business creation registration receipt
French tax/VAT number verification where applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the APE code is incorrect, apply to the competent statistical office through the Guichet unique for a rectification; if the K-bis or tax references are not received, contact the Greffe or the local DGFiP business registration unit and provide the RCS certificate to trigger prompt issuance.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: N/A — the public affairs and lobbying activity is not an industrial or manufacturing operation; the competent regulator is the Haute Autorité pour la Transparence de la Vie Publique (HATVP) for professional interest-representation registration.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Registre des représentants d'intérêts under Article 18-2 of Loi n° 2016-1691 (Sapin II Law) — mandatory electronic registration and annual action/disclosure declaration for lobbying and public affairs activity in France.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Direction Régionale de l'Environnement, de l'Aménagement et du Logement (DREAL) / Ministry of Ecological Transition (classification advisory only).
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — purely office-based administrative and advisory activity with no classified installation (ICPE threshold not exceeded) and no full EIA report required.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial discharges or VOCs are generated by the advisory office; waste must be managed under the Code de l'environnement, including separate collection of paper, IT equipment and batteries via registered waste channels, and office heating/cooling installations must comply with French energy and air-conditioning maintenance thresholds if applicable.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Office premises open to employees or the public must obtain a fire safety visit and favorable fire safety attestation from the competent safety commission for class 5 ERP premises where applicable; structural load inspection is not mandatory for standard offices unless the building has special structural risks; the SARL must maintain a Livret d'accueil or health and safety records for staff under the Labor Code.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP) via the official portal at impots.gouv.fr
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: French SARL entities are automatically assigned a SIREN/SIRET identifier upon registration with the French commercial registry (RCS) and Chambre des Métiers. Foreign-owned SARLs follow the standard incorporation procedure involving a French notary for the articles of association and subsequent tax authority notification.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box elections available under French law. Hybrid mismatch and controlled foreign company rules under ATAD Directive apply to prevent treaty shopping and base erosion.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory e-invoicing for large enterprises (turnover >25M EUR) via the French tax portal; real-time VAT clearance through PEP system with digital fiscal stamps for compliant invoicing.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rated exports of goods outside the EU or to certain destinations; for offshore services, zero-rating applies to supplies to non-EU clients with place of supply outside EU, supported by contractual evidence and payment proof.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration, Bill of Lading, Inward Remittance Certificate
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Claims for zero-rating must be substantiated; fraudulent or unsubstantiated claims lead to penalties of up to 80% of the VAT amount plus interest and potential criminal liability with retrospective clawback of benefits.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France (Bank of France), acting jointly with the Direction Générale du Trésor (French Treasury) of the Ministry of Economy, Finance and Industrial and Digital Sovereignty for exchange-control authorisations under Articles L.151-1 et seq. of the French Monetary and Financial Code (Code Monétaire et Financier – CMF), and the Autorité de Contrôle Prudentiel et de Résolution (ACPR) as the prudential supervisor and AML/CFT licensing authority for banks and electronic-money institutions operating in France.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: France is a Eurozone Member State; the euro (EUR) is domestic legal tender and is fully and freely convertible. Current-account convertibility for advisory retainer fees and lobbying service fees is unrestricted for EU/EEA counterparties. For non-EU/EEA counterparties, settlement of current-account operations is free from prior authorisation provided payment is channelled through an ACPR-licensed authorised intermediary and is covered by balance-of-payments reporting. Capital-account convertibility is equally preserved, but the restored French exchange-control regime (Finance Act 2020, Decree No. 2020-1549, CMF Articles L.151-1 to L.151-4) imposes a prior-authorisation threshold of EUR 1,500,000 per beneficiary/counterparty cluster per calendar year for defined 'financial relations' with non-EU/EEA states, including loans, guarantees, deposits, securities issues and foreign-exchange operations. Intra-EU/EEA capital movements are protected under the TFEU freedom-of-capital and cleared through TARGET2. Profit remittance for a French SARL is not a hard currency hurdle: dividends are paid from after-corporate-tax profits (IS at French standard rate 25%) and, when paid to non-resident shareholders, are subject to the French 25% dividend withholding tax (or 29.7% individual levy where applicable) unless reduced by a double-tax treaty or the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive (0% at qualifying holding thresholds). No foreign-exchange approval attaches to dividend distribution.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Historically French export-surrender obligations were abolished with the adoption of the euro; no mandatory conversion ratio or surrender requirement exists for export proceeds or service-export income. A French SARL may lawfully receive retainers from non-resident clients in EUR or in any freely convertible foreign currency, maintain non-EUR denominated accounts, and deploy those funds without any forced conversion quota. The binding statutory constraints are: (i) all inward proceeds must be received through an authorised intermediary bank so that Banque de France balance-of-payments statistical reporting is effected (individual transaction reporting at or above EUR 50,000 per operation, plus the monthly/quarterly direct-reporting aggregation thresholds applicable to enterprises); (ii) cross-border services exchanges (including government-affairs advisory) must be declared under the French 'Déclaration d'Échanges de Services' (DES) programme when the annual value per non-EU partner country exceeds the applicable exemption floor (currently EUR 250,000 per calendar year, as adjusted by customs order); and (iii) proceeds originating from jurisdictions subject to enhanced vigilance or sanctions will trigger additional AML/CFT controls and, where required, a declaration to TRACFIN. No percentage of export/service proceeds must be surrendered or converted into EUR.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account (compte courant; multi-currency EUR/USD rider available)
Operational Account (compte courant; dedicated retainer collection sub-account)

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Crédit Industriel et Commercial S.A. (CIC, Crédit Mutuel Alliance Fédérale)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account (compte courant; trade-liability and subscription clearing account)

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Crédit Agricole S.A. / Crédit Agricole Corporate & Investment Bank
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account (compte de dépôt; no capital escrow applicable post-incorporation)
Operational Account (compte courant; treasury and FX hedging settlement account)
Operational Account (compte courant; cross-border EUR/USD/GBP clearing rails)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Low-to-Medium as a primary treasury rail; Medium only as a secondary collection or disbursement channel. Legal constraints: any electronic-money institution (EMI) serving a French-resident corporate client must be authorised in France by the ACPR under CMF Articles L.525-1 et seq., or must passport into France from another EU/EEA state under the revised E-Money Directive (2009/110/EC, as amended by PSD2). Post-Brexit UK-chartered EMIs and US/offshore fintechs hold no standalone right to operate in France and cannot be used by a French SARL for settlement of non-EU receipts without an ACPR-licensed banking partner, because the French authorised-intermediary rule requires cross-border current-account settlements to pass through an authorised credit institution. The ISIC 7020 lobbying scope is classified as 'Medium_Risk_Enhanced' under FATF-based French typologies, so most automated-KYC EMIs decline onboarding; an EU-passported EMI with a full corporate UBO dossier and a French correspondent bank may be acceptable for low-value retainer collections, but the principal treasury account should remain with a Tier-1 French commercial bank.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For a French SARL with non-resident beneficial owners whose business purpose is cross-border trade policy and lobbying, French incumbent banks applying ACPR guidelines and Sapin II transparency controls will, de facto, require an in-person interview with the resident gérant (statutory manager) and at least one attestation interview with the ultimate beneficial owner before account activation. Remote onboarding is legally possible in France using eIDAS-compliant Qualified Electronic Signatures and ANSSI-certified identity verification, but it is not realistically available from Tier-1 legacy institutions for a Medium_Risk_Enhanced government-affairs client; neo-banks offering video-identity onboarding usually lack the compliance appetite for politically exposed counterparties. Where the foreign shareholder cannot travel, the acceptable substitute is a notarised and apostilled power of attorney in favour of the local gérant, a French sworn translation, certified passport copies and a structured video-identity session; however, the default mandate is physical presence for at least one director or duly authorised officer.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident shareholder or controlling individual screened as a Politically Exposed Person (PEP) or a foreign state official, triggering enhanced due diligence and potential Organs?/TRACFIN reporting.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: UBO declaration filed with the Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs (RBE), group/corporate ownership chart evidencing the full chain to ultimate individuals, PEP status disclosure with basis-of-wealth statement, certified source-of-funds evidence from the retainer/financing agreement, notarised and apostilled statutes, board resolution authorising account opening, certified passports and good-standing certificates, and three-year banking references from the home-jurisdiction bank.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Foreign-government-tied lobbying mandate and retainers from sovereign states or state-owned entities, raising corruption and foreign-influence risk under Sapin II law No. 2016-1691 and the EU Transparency Register framework.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Valid statutory operating licence and HATVP (Haute Autorité pour la Transparence de la Vie Publique) registration as a 'représentant d'intérêts', EU Transparency Register ID where applicable, executed client retainer agreement defining the lawful lobbying scope, conflict-of-interest and anti-bribery warranties, no-cash and no-private-payment policy, AML/CFT procedure manual incorporating Sapin II, detailed invoice trail and activity declaration showing no direct payments to public officials.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Recurring inbound wire transfers from non-EU high-risk or FATF-monitored jurisdictions for advisory services, creating unexplained-wealth suspicion and sanctions-list overmatching.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full client-file KYC package (corporate documents, UBO, bank references), sanctions screening evidence against the EU Consolidated List and prudent OFAC checks, documented economic rationale for each retainer, purpose-code classification and payment-chain invoice reconciliation, and enhanced monitoring records demonstrating that funds flow only from contractual counterparties; file a TRACFIN declaration if any doubt subsists.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Deficient or inconsistent foreign corporate documentation, notably missing apostille, French legalisation or disagreement between UBO declarations and bank beneficial-owner registers.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete notarised corporate bundle: memorandum/articles of association with certified French translation, French RCS-Kbis extract after registration, RBE receipt, INSEE/URSSAF/SIRET registration documents, French tax registration certificate, apostilled certificate of incorporation and good standing from the home registry, plus a French expert-comptable engagement letter confirming the economic substance and statutory location of the SARL.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant routing for inbound capital injection from non-resident shareholders: (i) open an operational EUR account with an ACPR-licensed French bank or, for cash capital increases/changes, a blocked 'compte bloqué' with the bank, Caisse des Dépôts, or a notary until the RCS registration is updated; (ii) instruct the sending bank to issue a SWIFT MT103 with beneficiary FR_SARL, the French IBAN, the bank BIC, and a clear economic reference such as 'INVESTISSEMENT DIRECT / APPORT EN CAPITAL' to allow Banque de France classification as direct-investment capital; (iii) supply the bank with the board/shareholder resolution approving the capital increase, the updated certified articles, source-of-funds attestation and the French INSEE/Kbis dossier; (iv) for non-EU injections exceeding EUR 1,500,000 in aggregate in one calendar year, obtain the French Treasury prior authorisation before crediting the second tranche; and (v) where the remitting jurisdiction is on the FATF or EU denial-of-authorisation list, complete enhanced due diligence and independently verify the economic rationale before acceptance. The receiving bank automatically performs balance-of-payments declaration to Banque de France; the SARL must preserve the banking reference so that tax and audit records match the declared purpose code.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For outbound trade disbursements related to retainer pass-through fees, international advocacy payments and subcontractor advisers, the primary clearing rails are: (i) SEPA Credit Transfer (SCT) and SEPA Instant for EUR-denominated payments within the EU/EEA; (ii) SWIFT MT103 (with GPI tracking) for non-EU wire settlements, carrying an ISO 20022 purpose-code classification for professional advisory services and the French BIC/IBAN identification; and (iii) UCP600-compliant Commercial Letters of Credit only where the underlying contract expressly requires documentary settlement for trade-policy advisory milestones, although in practice a clean payment against signed retainer and invoice is the prevailing instrument. Where a Bank Payment Obligation (BPO) is proposed, it is legally permissible but commercially marginal for ISIC 7020 services. All outbound settlements must be executed by an authorised French intermediary, must not breach EU sanctions/embargo rules, and must contain a full payment-reference chain so that operations above EUR 50,000 per beneficiary per transaction are automatically reported to Banque de France for balance-of-payments statistics.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable FX forwards on EUR/USD, EUR/GBP, EUR/CHF and EUR/CNY, tenor-matched to contracted retainer receivables or supplier payables and documented with a real underlying exposure.
FX swaps (changes de devises / swaps cambistes) for temporary conversion and reconversion of non-EUR retainers or disbursement floats through the ACPR-licensed treasury booking bank.
Cross-currency interest-rate swaps (CCS/CRS) under an ISDA master agreement to hedge intra-group shareholder loans or acquisition financings carrying EUR/USD and reference-rate exposure.

Vanilla European-style FX options (calls and puts) on major convertible pairs, purchased solely for downside protection on forecast advisory-currency income and confirmed under a standard FX master agreement.

Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) are not permissible for EUR-based underlyings in France because the euro is freely convertible and fully deliverable; a French resident treasury cannot book NDFs for EUR unless the counterparty currency is itself restricted, a situation not presented by this SARL.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual accounts filing (dépôt des comptes annuels) with shareholder approval and meeting minutes
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce via the Infogreffe e-filing platform
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after the close of the financial year; for calendar-year entities, by 30 June of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing triggers a monetary sanction of up to €7,500 for legal persons, possible court-ordered injunction with daily penalties (astreinte), and repeated omission may lead to administrative strike-off (radiation) from the RCS.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual beneficial-owner declaration / update (déclaration des bénéficiaires effectifs)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce via the RCS / Infogreffe system
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within fifteen days after any change in beneficial ownership; otherwise confirmed as current at the time of the annual accounts filing and the AGM approving the accounts
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Persistent non-disclosure or incomplete UBO information may be sanctioned by administrative fines under the French Monetary and Financial Code and can block the registration and continued listing of the company at the RCS.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate income tax return bundle (liasse fiscale, including form n°2065/2065-SD and supporting schedules)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Direction générale des Finances publiques (DGFiP) via online e-filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a company with a 31 December year-end, by May 15 of the following year; for off-calendar year-ends, within three months after the closing date according to the DGFiP e-filing calendar
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing incurs a 10% surcharge if filed within 30 days of the due date and 40% thereafter, plus monthly late-payment interest of 0.2% on unpaid corporate income tax; non-refusal can escalate to administrative penalties and loss of deduction rights.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual declaration of interest-representation activities (déclaration annuelle du représentant d'intérêts)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Haute Autorité pour la Transparence de la Vie Publique (HATVP) online register
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by the anniversary date of the initial registration in the HATVP register; supplementary semestral reporting may apply for active lobbying engagements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to submit or materially inaccurate declarations expose the company to an administrative financial sanction of up to €30,000, scoring on the public register, and potential removal from the lobbying register.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual business-value tax declaration and tax-type confirmation for fixed business premises (Cotisation Foncière des Entreprises, CFE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Declaration due by May 15 for calendar-year taxpayers or per the published DGFiP schedule; payment of the CFE liability generally falls due by December 15 of the same year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing or payment attracts an automatic 10% surcharge plus interest at 0.2% per month; failure to pay the CFE for two consecutive years can activate collection enforcement and loss of tax clean-hands status for public tenders or lobbying authorization.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A statutory auditor (commissaire aux comptes) is mandatory if the SARL exceeds two of the three following thresholds at the close of the financial year: balance-sheet total above €4,000,000; turnover excluding tax above €8,000,000; average number of employees above 50. An audit may also be required for controlled or consolidating affiliates or under specific regulatory regimes.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Statutory individual accounts must be prepared in accordance with French GAAP (Plan Comptable Général) as codified in the Code de Commerce; IFRS is optional only for consolidated financial statements or where parent-entity rules require it, and is not the primary standard for SARL individual statutory accounts.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The SARL must file an initial declaration of beneficial owners with the RCS and update it within 15 days of any shareholding or control change. Share transfers in a SARL require an update of the register of shareholders and, if a paper-based agreement exists, registration of the transfer, as well as payment of the registration duty within one month. In the annual corporate cycle, the shareholders approving the accounts confirm the current list of members and managers; if the beneficial-owner data has changed without a corresponding RCS update, the company must submit the revised UBO declaration no later than the date of the annual accounts filing.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% corporate income tax (impôt sur les sociétés) for standard taxable profits.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Eligible small and medium-sized companies may apply a 15% rate on the first EUR 42,500 of taxable profit, generally subject to turnover not exceeding EUR 10 million, paid-up capital and ownership conditions. Eligible research and development expenditure may qualify for a 30% French research tax credit up to EUR 100 million of qualifying expenditure and 5% above that threshold. Other sector-specific credits, accelerated deductions and temporary incentives may apply only if statutory conditions are satisfied.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Unlimited carryforward period, subject to the annual utilization cap of EUR 1 million plus 50% of the portion of taxable profit exceeding EUR 1 million. The unused balance may generally be carried back to the immediately preceding financial year, subject to statutory limits and election requirements.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 2065-SD, corporate income tax return, filed with the corporate tax package through the French tax administration professional portal (espace professionnel) using EFI or, generally for companies and tax intermediaries, EDI-TDFC. The return is accompanied by forms 2050-SD through 2059-SD and applicable supporting schedules.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual return; corporate income tax installments are generally paid quarterly, with a final balance payment.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For a financial year ending on a date other than 31 December, filing is generally due within three months after the end of the financial year. For a 31 December year-end, filing is generally due on the second business day after 1 May of the following year. The French tax administration may publish the applicable electronic filing date for the relevant year. Corporate income tax installments are generally due on 15 March, 15 June, 15 September and 15 December, with a final balance generally due by the 15th day of the fourth month after year-end; a 31 December year-end generally has a 15 May balance deadline.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name, SIREN number, registered office, tax office, financial year dates, legal form as Société à Responsabilité Limitée, principal activity and contact details.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident shareholder or parent is not entered as the taxpayer unless it itself operates through a French permanent establishment. The French SARL files using its own SIREN and French tax registration details.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable profit or loss, applicable corporate income tax rate, tax due, tax credits, withholding credits, installment payments and balance payable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include all profits attributable to the French company. Transactions with non-resident related parties must be reflected consistently with the arm's-length result and documented under French transfer pricing rules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reconciliation from accounting profit to taxable profit, including non-deductible expenses, exempt income, provisions, depreciation adjustments, tax credits and other permanent or temporary differences.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Disallow expenses that do not satisfy French deductibility rules, including certain excessive interest, non-business expenditure, penalties and expenses lacking adequate evidence or business purpose.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax losses carried forward or carried back, current-year loss utilization and remaining loss balances.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Track losses at the French company level. A foreign group company's losses cannot be used by the SARL absent a specific French consolidation or restructuring regime.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax credits, reductions and amounts carried forward, including eligible research and development credits where applicable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim only credits supported by statutory eligibility, contemporaneous expenditure records and required declarations. Foreign expenditure is not automatically qualifying.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Financial, capital gain, participation and other tax adjustments where relevant.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report cross-border disposals, participation income, restructurings and related-party adjustments under the applicable French rules and treaty provisions.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: 2050-SD to 2053-SD, balance sheet and income statement
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: French tax-package balance sheet, profit and loss account, fixed assets, depreciation, provisions, receivables, liabilities and accounting result.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The accounts must reconcile to the statutory French accounts and the filed 2065-SD. Intercompany balances should agree with the counterparties' records and transfer pricing schedules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Form 2067-SD, payments to related or specified recipients
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Certain payments such as commissions, brokerage, fees, royalties and other specified remuneration exceeding applicable reporting thresholds.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report payments to foreign recipients where the form and threshold rules apply, regardless of whether the recipient is a group company.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Annual summary of controlled transactions, transfer pricing method, foreign jurisdictions and documentation status for entities meeting the applicable EUR 50 million turnover or gross-assets threshold, or belonging to an applicable group.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A French subsidiary of a foreign group must file where the statutory threshold or group conditions are met. The declaration does not replace full transfer pricing documentation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Electronic payment of installments and final corporate income tax balance using the company's tax account and payment mandate.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Payments must be made by the French taxpayer or its authorized representative. Foreign shareholders are not substitutes for the SARL's French tax payment obligations.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late or incomplete filing generally attracts a 10% surcharge, potentially increased to 40% after formal notice and 80% in cases involving fraudulent maneuvers or abuse of rights. Late-payment interest is generally 0.20% per month, subject to statutory exceptions and calculation rules; France does not generally impose a separate daily corporate income tax surcharge. Tax assessments may include the underlying tax, interest and penalties. Failure to file transfer pricing documentation can trigger a specific penalty generally equal to the greater of EUR 10,000 or 0.5% of the transactions covered by the missing or incomplete documentation, subject to applicable statutory limits.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% French withholding tax generally applies to dividends and similar distributions paid by a French company to a non-resident corporate recipient, subject to domestic exemptions, European Union rules and applicable tax treaties. A 12.8% rate generally applies to distributions paid to non-resident individual taxpayers, subject to treaty and domestic-law provisions.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Before payment, obtain a valid certificate of tax residence from the recipient's foreign tax authority and complete the applicable French forms, commonly Form 5000-SD together with Form 5001-SD for dividend income or the relevant treaty schedule. Submit the documentation to the French payer or withholding agent within the prescribed timing so that treaty relief can be applied at source where permitted. If relief was not applied, the recipient may generally seek a refund from the French tax administration using the prescribed forms and supporting evidence. The French-EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive may provide a withholding exemption for qualifying corporate shareholders, commonly requiring a minimum participation, minimum holding-period commitment, subject-to-tax status and anti-abuse compliance. Treaty entitlement depends on the specific bilateral convention, beneficial ownership, limitation-on-benefits or principal-purpose provisions and anti-conduit rules.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties and similar payments to non-residents may generally be subject to French withholding at up to 25% under domestic rules, with possible reductions or exemptions under an applicable treaty or the EU Interest and Royalties Directive if all conditions are met. Interest paid by a French company to a non-resident is generally not subject to ordinary French withholding tax, although exceptions apply, including certain payments to non-cooperative or listed jurisdictions, anti-abuse situations and specific financial instruments. Treaty rates vary by recipient, beneficial ownership, income classification and residence state; the relevant bilateral treaty must be reviewed before payment.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EUR 400 million threshold for full French transfer pricing documentation generally applies where the French entity's annual pre-tax turnover or gross assets reach at least EUR 400 million, where it belongs to a group meeting that threshold, or where it is controlled by or controls an entity meeting the statutory conditions. A simplified annual transfer pricing declaration generally applies from EUR 50 million of turnover or gross assets, subject to additional statutory conditions. Local File and Master File content must be available in the required French or accepted language and produced within the statutory response period.
approved_arm_length_methodologies: Other OECD-consistent methods where the selected method is the most appropriate for the transaction and is adequately supported
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: France does not operate a standalone economic substance regime equivalent to the substance regulations of certain international financial centres. Substance remains relevant under the French general anti-abuse rule, abuse-of-law doctrine, beneficial ownership analysis, controlled foreign company rules, permanent establishment principles, interest limitation rules, EU anti-hybrid rules and treaty principal-purpose tests. A French SARL conducting government-affairs advisory and lobbying work should maintain French operational substance proportionate to its functions, including genuine personnel or decision-making capacity, premises or operational infrastructure, client files, engagement evidence, documented board decisions, banking control and commercially defensible remuneration.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Concealing lobbying or advisory revenue, issuing false invoices, maintaining undisclosed accounts, fabricating expenses, diverting company receipts or intentionally understating taxable profit.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Assessment of unpaid tax, late-payment interest and penalties; serious tax fraud may lead to criminal fines and imprisonment, including aggravated tax fraud penalties that can reach seven years' imprisonment and EUR 3 million for individuals, subject to statutory conditions and judicial findings.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Managers may incur criminal liability, civil liability for intentional misconduct, tax penalties and liability for fraudulent or seriously negligent conduct contributing to tax non-payment. Travel restrictions or asset seizures may occur through judicial or enforcement procedures. Corporate veil piercing is exceptional and is not automatic merely because the company is insolvent.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: False Transfer Pricing and Profit Diversion
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Charging non-arm's-length management, lobbying, referral, royalty or financing fees to foreign affiliates; allocating French functions to an offshore entity without evidence; or using sham service agreements to shift profits.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Corporate income tax reassessment, withholding tax exposure, interest, penalties for deliberate understatements or abuse of rights, and specific sanctions for missing or materially deficient transfer pricing documentation. A French tax authority adjustment may also trigger corresponding foreign tax disputes.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be personally exposed where they knowingly approve sham arrangements, fraudulent records or abusive distributions. Ordinary commercial transfer pricing errors do not by themselves pierce the corporate veil.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Conducting lobbying activities before covered French public officials without required registration with the Haute Autorité pour la Transparence de la Vie Publique, failing to disclose lobbying actions, submitting inaccurate information or breaching applicable ethical obligations.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative publication, compliance measures and criminal sanctions may apply depending on the breach. Certain failures to comply with HATVP obligations can result in imprisonment and fines under the French transparency legislation; the precise sanction depends on the prohibited conduct and status of the actor.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Responsible managers and individual lobbyists may be prosecuted personally. A director is not automatically liable for every employee breach, but authorization, instruction, concealment or failure to implement reasonable controls can support personal civil or criminal exposure.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Bribery, Influence Peddling and Public-Sector Corruption
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Offering, promising, authorizing or recording payments, gifts, employment, commissions or other benefits to influence a public official, elected representative, public procurement decision or administrative outcome.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal prosecution may result in substantial fines, imprisonment, confiscation, exclusion from public contracts and corporate penalties. French anti-corruption law applies to conduct connected with France and may have extraterritorial reach in specified circumstances.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, beneficial owners, employees and intermediaries can be personally prosecuted. Corporate liability may coexist with individual liability; proceeds and assets may be frozen or confiscated. Travel restrictions can be imposed by judicial order where legally justified.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Accepting opaque retainer wires, unexplained third-party payments, cash or crypto proceeds, success fees linked to public decisions, or funds from high-risk jurisdictions without customer due diligence, beneficial-owner verification, sanctions screening and suspicious-transaction escalation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Supervisory, administrative and criminal measures may include fines, professional restrictions, confiscation, tax reassessment and imprisonment for money laundering or terrorist-financing conduct. Suspicious activity reporting obligations apply where the entity falls within a regulated or legally designated category; contractual and bank compliance obligations may apply more broadly.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Managers and compliance officers may be liable for knowingly participating in laundering, facilitating prohibited payments or deliberately ignoring red flags. Individual sanctions may include imprisonment, fines, confiscation and judicial travel restrictions.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Providing policy, government-relations or strategic advisory services to sanctioned persons, restricted governments or prohibited sectors, or routing payments through intermediaries to evade EU or French sanctions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Asset freezes, transaction prohibitions, administrative or criminal fines, confiscation and imprisonment may apply. Banking relationships may be terminated and the company may be excluded from public or regulated engagements.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and employees who authorize or knowingly facilitate circumvention may face personal criminal liability. Internal delegation does not eliminate responsibility where senior management knew or should have known of the prohibited transaction.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Improper Dividend, Capital or Related-Party Distribution
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Distributing profits without distributable reserves, paying disguised dividends through inflated related-party fees, returning capital contrary to statutory procedures or making distributions while concealing insolvency.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Repayment of unlawful distributions, corporate and shareholder claims, tax reassessment, withholding tax exposure, management liability and possible criminal consequences for unlawful dividend distribution or fraudulent insolvency conduct.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Managers may be required to restore improperly distributed amounts and compensate creditors or the company. Personal exposure is heightened where accounts were knowingly false, distributions were knowingly unlawful or insolvency was aggravated by management misconduct.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Permanent Establishment and Unreported French Activity
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the SARL, a foreign affiliate or individual consultants to conduct sustained French commercial activity while reporting the functions, contracts or profits in another jurisdiction, or treating French personnel as independent agents without factual support.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: French corporate income tax, payroll and VAT assessments, withholding tax, interest, penalties and possible double-tax treaty disputes. The tax authority may recharacterize the arrangement based on actual functions and authority rather than contractual labels.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may face liability for deliberate concealment or fraudulent records. Failure to register or account for a French taxable presence may also generate civil, administrative and employment-law consequences, but ordinary classification disputes do not automatically create personal liability.
